event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Semis and energy led; breadth broke, defensives cracked.
SOXX +2.83% carried the week while DIA -1.23% and XLV -2.65% lagged; Friday's non-farm payroll miss (2.9 vs 9.0 forecast) capped a week of softening labor data that never stopped the semis bid. The tape split cleanly in two: AI hardware and energy up, everything rate-sensitive and defensive down.

INDICES — SOXX +2.83%, QQQ +0.68%, IJH +0.55%, IJR +0.17%, IWM -0.16%, SPY -0.22%, RSP -0.65%, DIA -1.23%. Large beat small by 0.51pp, but the real gap was semis versus everything. VIX at 15.3, below its 15.9 20-day average — vol fell while the median stock fell. Biggest cross-asset move: silver SLV -5.85% for the week, with gold GLD -3.37% and WTI USO +3.72% (20d). 42% of S&P names sit above their 200-day MA; IWM and RSP are both below theirs.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLK +1.80%, XLE +1.26%, XLU +0.81%, XLI -0.28%, XLY -0.47%, XLRE -1.80%, XLP -1.86%, XLB -1.89%, XLC -2.34%, XLF -2.46%, XLV -2.65%. Top industries: SMH +3.96% and CIBR +3.71%; bottom: MSOS -13.37% and SILJ -6.81%. Money moved out of XLF (-$2,305mm, 0th percentile) and XLV (-$1,089mm) into XLY (+$711mm, 100th percentile) and XLK; at the index level, DIA +$1,971mm and SOXX +$1,797mm took in while SPY bled -$13,002mm. Rotation state: narrow mega-cap tape.

DRIVERS — Semis absorbed the week's flows (SOXX +2.83%, SMH +3.96%), and the labor data cut both ways: September payrolls at 2.9 versus 9.0 forecast, unemployment 4.2%, average hourly earnings +0.1% versus +0.30% — a soft print that pushed rate-cut odds to 82% on Polymarket for October. That bid duration-adjacent risk while gutting financials and healthcare. Silver's -5.85% and gold's -3.37% week says the metal complex unwound from a crowded long, not a macro signal. Breadth was ugly: 61 new 60-day lows against 19 highs, only 25% of S&P names above their 50-day MA.

WHAT'S NEXT — ISM Non-Manufacturing Monday (forecast 55.7 vs prior 55.4) is the first test of whether soft labor data bleeds into services; a strong print would let the semis trade run. Watch SOXX gamma around its 100th-percentile flow week — a crowded long into a 4-day week on taper. XLV's -2.65% with $1,089mm of outflow is the contrarian setup; a stabilization in healthcare would be the first sign of a broadening tape.
